comment: Agent Package checker fixture (Common Agent 12.10, with 12.2 to 12.7 and the parts of Section 6 they cite). Every case is a package: the base package below with the case's edits applied in order. A set edit writes a file's text, a delete edit removes a file, a move edit renames a file, and a json edit sets (or, with remove, deletes) the member at a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) and writes the file back in the package's one spelling, two-space indented with a final newline. Where a case says rehash, the manifest's two digests are then recomputed over the two authored files, under whichever names the package uses; where it says regenerate, NOT.md, RECORDS.md and SYSTEMS.md are generated again from them. Both are done so that a case fails for its own reason and no other. The digest of a named run config, of a view's file, of an example's file and of a lockfile is written out in the case, because it is part of what the case says. The draft Descriptor is agent-descriptor.json; the runtime requirements are agent-runtime-requirements.json, pointed at under runtime_requirements, with format agent-runtime-requirements-v1. A checker reads each name used before 0.30.0-draft (descriptor.json, install.json, the pointer install, the format agent-install-v1) where the current one is absent, and prefers the current one where both are present (12.2); a valid case that says warnings gives the number of warnings a checker gives when it reports each former name, each pair, and each address literal in a script (the address check of 12.10). A checker MUST accept every valid case and MUST refuse every invalid one, and the check each invalid case names is one that refuses it. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation.
spec: SPEC.md at Common Agent 0.41.0: 12.10 (the checker and its address check), 12.2 (layout and the former names), 12.3 (the draft Descriptor), 12.4 and 12.4.1 (the runtime requirements and the model system), 12.5 (skills and the generated views), 12.6 (the rules), 12.7 (named run configs), 6.2 and 5.8 (a named run config and its digest), 6.13.4 (a setting's range and multiple), 6.13.6, 6.13.8 and 6.13.10 (the files a view and an example name), 6.14.4 and 6.14.8 (can_use)

checks.layout: the files of 12.2 are present, under their names or their former names, and the JSON files parse
checks.manifest: plugin.json validates against the pinned Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema, points at the two authored files by path and digest, is a draft, and carries an address only in $schema, homepage, repository and each from entry's repository
checks.descriptor: the draft Descriptor carries no subject, acts_for or shape, says what the agent refuses and records, and carries no address but the schema of each entry of its own can_use, which is read structurally (Section 12.6, rule 3)
checks.can-use: can_use is a list, and each entry has a schema that is an absolute https URL and that no other entry names, a non-empty reads, a does and a without (Section 6.14.8)
checks.offering: each offering passes the declaration checks of 6.11
checks.how-run: no job or step declares a how that 12.3 refuses, and every run sits on a job whose how allows one and uses only the placeholders 12.3 lists
checks.run-configs: every named run config sets only declared settings, with values each setting allows, under a name used once and a digest that matches its entry (Section 12.7)
checks.carried-files: each view's file and each example's file is in the package under the digest the Descriptor gives, at a path inside the package, and a view's file names no address (Section 6.13.10)
checks.runtime-requirements: the runtime requirements have their format and sections, no address of any kind, a kind from the four of 12.4 on every system, and well-formed job_seconds and answer
checks.model: at most one system has the kind model, its protocols are one or more from the list of Section 12.4.1, and its entry names no credential and no variable
checks.systems: the system names of the Descriptor and the runtime requirements are the same set, read through the role alias
checks.ceilings: every spending system has a ceiling, every ceiling names the side that enforces it, and a ceiling over a system the scripts reach with a named credential says runtime
checks.dependencies: every lockfile the runtime requirements name is in the package with the digest they give
checks.skills: one skill per offering and per step, no skill without one, and each SKILL.md carries name and description in its frontmatter
checks.mcp: every mcp.json server is a declared system, and mcp.json carries no address
checks.views: NOT.md, RECORDS.md and SYSTEMS.md match a fresh generation byte for byte
checks.hidden: no text file carries a zero-width character, a bidirectional control or a tag-block character

files.net.agentdoc.package/RECORDS.md:
# The records this agent must leave

This is the contract. The agent leaves the following behind, on
every run.

- the document as received — at `*/document`
- the brief as sent

An agent that leaves less than this does not do this job,
whatever else it does well.
files.net.agentdoc.package/SYSTEMS.md:
# The systems this agent needs

Named by what the work needs rather than by product. The access level
is the most this work needs; a deployment that grants more is granting
more than the job requires.

| System | Kind | Access | What the access is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| speech | service | trigger | to read the brief aloud; credential `speech-key`, spends per characters, the caller's material is sent to it |
| documents | directory | read | to read the document |

Whoever deploys this agent binds these systems to their own,
and places any named credential. Nothing here names a product.
